name: Pulmonary Hypertension Owing to Lung Disease and/or Hypoxia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESC/ERS Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Presence of underlying chronic lung disease and/or hypoxia documented by pulmonary function tests, imaging, or arterial blood gases
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as thromboembolic or left heart disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg with PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg in the presence of documented lung disease and/or hypoxia, excluding other causes of pulmonary hypertension
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Right heart catheterization is mandatory for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

pathognomonic.notes: Central or peripheral cyanosis due to hypoxemia

common.notes: Due to right heart strain or arrhythmias
Lower limb swelling from right heart failure
Shortness of breath when lying flat

occasional.notes: Transient loss or near loss of consciousness due to reduced cerebral perfusion
Coughing up blood due to pulmonary vascular changes
Due to hepatic congestion from right heart failure

rare.notes: Due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression by enlarged pulmonary artery
Visible neck vein distension from right heart failure

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and/or hypercapnia
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
imaging: Chest X-ray showing enlarged pulmonary arteries
High-resolution CT scan demonstrating underlying lung disease (e.g., interstitial lung disease, COPD)
Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; secondary to lung disease or hypoxia
other: Pulmonary function tests showing obstructive or restrictive lung disease

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of significant lung disease or hypoxia
Presence of idiopathic or heritable causes
Imaging evidence of chronic thromboembolic obstruction
Different treatment approach including possible surgical intervention

redFlags: Rapid progression of dyspnea and right heart failure symptoms
Syncope episodes indicating severe hemodynamic compromise
Signs of right ventricular failure such as ascites or severe peripheral edema
references: Galiè N, Humbert M, Vachiery JL, et al. 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2016 Jan 1;37(1):67-119.
Simonneau G, Montani D, Celermajer DS, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019 Jan;53(1):1801913.
